objectives.text: Get back an elected government. The Transitional Presidential Council, formed in April 2024 to hold power until an election or 7 February 2026, dissolved on that date with no presidential election held and no successor structure agreed. The prime minister, Alix Didier Fils-Aime, governs with the backing of Washington, which threatened 'serious consequences' against any move to oust him. The provisional electoral council (CEP) published a calendar on 27 July 2026 for a general election in December 2026 (13 December in the Wikipedia summary read, with a runoff on 21 February 2027 listed). The election is conditional on security and funding, and the 30 August date set earlier was dropped; elections have slipped since 2019, so the date is a target, not a fact.

objectives.text: Retake Port-au-Prince from the gang coalition Viv Ansanm with a foreign force, the Gang Suppression Force (GSF), authorised by the Security Council at up to 5,550 personnel. About 1,500 troops were in place when the mandate was renewed on 29 September 2026 (Reuters), and more than 2,000 by 22 October (AP); Reuters put the force at roughly a third of its planned size on 21 October. The Kenyan contingent is being replaced by Chadian troops, and Sri Lanka has also deployed soldiers.

means.text: A foreign-manned force, not a Haitian one: the GSF works with the Haitian National Police and the Armed Forces of Haiti. Personnel were pledged by Kenya (until its exit), Chad, Jamaica, the Bahamas, Guyana, Barbados, Antigua and Barbuda, Bangladesh and Benin. Pledges are not deployments; the troops in place are more than 2,000 (AP, 22 October), against about 1,500 reported at the renewal of the mandate on 29 September (Reuters). El Salvador is in the force too, with pilots and technical staff for medical evacuation by its president's account, and four of its personnel went missing after the ambush of 18 October (AP, 21 October).

constraints.text: The force is funded and staffed below plan and its contributors are leaving: Kenya brought its second contingent home in March 2026 and Chad is replacing it. Haiti's own police cannot yet hold the ground the force takes. The biggest attack on the force since it began operating came on 18 October in Croix-des-Bouquets, and the mission's envoy told the Security Council that the gangs were testing it, with reprisal killings and advances into Kenscoff and the Artibonite (AP, 19 October).

paradoxes.text: The foreign force that keeps the capital from falling to the gangs also keeps the Haitian police and army from being rebuilt, since the GSF is the security. When the contributors leave, the gap returns to the streets; the security bought from outside is what makes the interim survivable, and the interim is what should have built Haitian security.

grand_strategy.reading:
Haiti's grand strategy is to get back an elected government and to retake Port-au-Prince, and it pays for both by renting its security from a UN-authorised foreign force (Kenya first, now Chad and others) and by living on remittances that tie it to its diaspora and to the United States. The transition ended on 7 February 2026 without an election or a successor, and the prime minister now governs on Washington's backing, while the force holds about a third of its authorised strength and its own police are not yet rebuilt. Not verified for this card: cholera and famine, which were asked for as constraints but for which no source was reached within the budget, the CARICOM mediation, the OAS and UN positions beyond the mission, and the Dominican wall.

After the ambush of 18 October in Croix-des-Bouquets, which left four Salvadoran technicians of the force missing, and El Salvador's rescue announcement of 21 October, the attack shows the gangs testing the foreign force the interim rents its security from. As of 25 October no rescue or release was confirmed: remains handed over at Port-au-Prince airport were disputed by President Bukele, who said they were not the four men. The electoral council's calendar of 27 July, which puts a general election in December 2026, is conditional on the same security.

stances.note: Viv Ansanm, formed in September 2023 by G9 and G-Pèp, was created to attack the Haitian government (police stations, government buildings, infrastructure) and to fight the international force (Wikipedia, tier 4). Adversary is our reading, not a source's word, and it is the rare grade by design: the sources show hostile attacks on the state, not a stated aim of replacing it, so if a stricter reading is taken this becomes rival. Bond none: no kinship or affinity is named. Trend stable: the 2026 coverage shows continued killings, with no sign of a turn. Trend moved to cooling on 29 October 2026 on the events of 18-21 October: gangs attacked the force in Croix-des-Bouquets and left four Salvadoran technicians missing, which El Salvador says the gangs hold (AP, 21 Oct); the mission's envoy told the Security Council that the gangs were testing the force, with reprisal killings and advances into Kenscoff and the Artibonite (AP, 19 Oct). Cooling here means the hostility is hardening; the grade stays adversary.

stances.note: Washington is the patron of the post-transition arrangement: it backed Prime Minister Fils-Aime staying on after the council's mandate ended on 7 February 2026, threatened serious consequences against any removal and sanctioned five council members (Reuters, via Citizen Digital). Its funding of the force is not confirmed by any source reached here, so it is not stated. It is the major trading partner under HOPE and HELP (Wikipedia). Cooling is our reading from the 2026 terminations: the US has moved to end Temporary Protected Status for Haitians, and the Supreme Court in June 2026 let the termination for Haiti proceed (Wikipedia, tier 4). Partner, not ally: transactional and interest-based. Bond none: no source names a kinship or an open wound between the pair. The since date is the 2026 backing; the trade partnership is older. Confidence C.

stances.note: Relations have long been hostile: since Haiti's independence in 1804 the two states have had wars, massacres, border disputes and stand-offs, and migration keeps tension high in the 21st century (Wikipedia, tier 4). Rival is our reading: the sources show friction and no declared aim of destroying the other state. Bond grievance: the historical wounds are open and the migration dispute is ongoing. The Dominican Republic's measures against Haitian migrants are the current friction; the card does not assess them further, and the DOM card is in progress and not read here. Trend stable is provisional. Confidence C.

stances.note: Added 29 October 2026 in the delta pass on the events of 18-21 October. El Salvador has personnel in the Gang Suppression Force: pilots and technical staff for medical evacuation, by the account of President Bukele (AP, 21 Oct). Four of them went missing after the gang ambush of 18 October in Croix-des-Bouquets; El Salvador announced a rescue operation on 21 October, and more special forces reached Haiti on 22 October (Tico Times, 25 Oct). Grade partner: a contributor to a UN-authorised force, with no treaty or alliance named in the sources, so this is our reading (confidence C). Trend warming: the Haitian government called the captives its foremost concern and said it was deploying all the assets needed (AP, 21 Oct). The since date is the first report of the Salvadoran contingent in the sources read, not the start of that deployment, which the sources do not date. Bond none: no shared identity or open wound is named.

stances_toward.note: Our reading (C). Santo Domingo cooperates in the Haitian security mission (the Dominican foreign minister announced the Chadian rotation that replaces the Kenyan force) while resisting alignment with Haiti's state: the April 2025 package adds a 1,500-soldier border reinforcement, an accelerated wall and tougher penalties for migrant smugglers. The grade is reluctant_partner, not rival, because no source read calls the relation hostile. Trend cooling: the border measures harden over 2025-26. Bond grievance is our reading and stays unsourced for now: the historical wound between the two states is not in any source read yet, so it needs a source before the bond is treated as confirmed.
